The bidding guidelines, schemes, and contractual arrangements cannot override or modify statutory regulations framed by the Commission under Section 178 of the Electricity Act, 2003, and the Petitioner's reliance on MNRE guidelines to seek re-classification under DSM Regulations is legally misconceived and unsustainable.

## **<u>Rejoinder by the Petitioner, Vena Energy, dated 18.02.2026, on the Reply submitted by the Respondent No. 1, SRPC</u>**

- (d) SRPC itself acknowledged in the Reply that the PPA dated 03.05.2021 recognises and refers to the Petitioner as a Wind Power Developer. The said contractual recognition was not incidental; it flows directly from the policy framework of the 2020 Blended Wind Guidelines, which mandates a predominant wind component and permits limited solar blending only as an ancillary measure.

- (a) In the present case, the Petitioner’s Blended Wind Power Project, having a predominantly wind-based character, is materially and fundamentally distinct from a hybrid project. It is a settled principle that unequal cannot be treated equally.

- (b) The Petitioner’s sole and limited grievance pertains to classification, namely that a project conceived, bid and commissioned under the MNRE’s Blended Wind Scheme and the 2020 Blended Wind Guidelines, which permit limited solar blending up to 20%, has been categorised as a “generating station based on solar or a hybrid of wind-solar resources” under the DSM Regulations, 2024, despite being a predominantly wind-based Project. The Petitioner sought only correct classification, so that the deviation tolerance bands and settlement principles are applied equitably with the governing statutory and policy framework.
